description: Disk defragmenter and optimizer: puts folders at the start of the disk and big, rarely used files (SpaceHogs) at the end, or sorts files by name, size or date.
notes: JkDefrag 3.36 (2008) by Jeroen Kessels, the last open source version; its successor MyDefrag is closed source.
Not developed since; written for Windows XP and Vista, it works through the standard Windows defragmentation API.
The files come from PortableApps.com's JkDefrag Portable 3.36 Rev 2, without its launcher.
Command: 'jkdefrag' (JkDefrag64.exe on 64-bit Windows), from an elevated terminal, e.g.
Without a drive it processes ALL fixed drives. Options: -a (action), -u (SpaceHogs mask), -e (exclude mask), -l (log file).
The 'JkDefrag' shortcut in Scoop Apps opens PortableApps.com's small GUI (pick drives, then Analyze, Defragment
or Defragment and Optimize). The shortcut is set to run as administrator: started without admin rights,
the GUI restarts itself elevated in C:\Windows\System32 and then cannot find JkDefrag. 'scoop reset' recreates
the shortcut without that setting; run 'scoop update JkDefrag -f' afterwards to set it again.
Some antivirus programs flag JkDefragGUI.exe because it is a compiled AutoIt script.
post_install: # JkDefragGUI.exe uses #RequireAdmin and finds JkDefrag(64).exe and its languages folder relative to the
# working folder. Started without admin rights, it restarts itself elevated in System32 and fails, so the
# shortcut gets the 'Run as administrator' flag (SLDF_RUNAS_USER, 0x2000 in LinkFlags at offset 0x14),
# which elevates it at once and keeps the shortcut's working folder.
